title: A Walk with a Flower Seller
theme: Six stops from Ludgate Hill down to the river with Nell Baker, who sells violets and watercress outside St Paul's. London in the spring of 1850: the busiest city on earth, the Crystal Palace rising in Hyde Park for next year's Great Exhibition, cholera two summers behind them and coming back, the new railways, the old river. Told from the pavement, not the palace.

companion.name: Nell Baker
companion.role: Flower seller, Covent Garden and Ludgate Hill
companion.brief: Thirty-one, widowed, two children (Tom, nine, and Sal, six). Buys violets, wallflowers and watercress at Covent Garden before six and sells from a basket on Ludgate Hill. Born in Clerkenwell. Sharp, warm, funny. SHE IS THE TOUR'S HOST AND NARRATOR: she speaks like the finest kind of broadcast presenter of a guided walk - welcoming, vivid, always carrying the listener forward to the next thing - but she is entirely a woman of 1850 and uses only the language, measures and ideas of her time. She addresses the visitor directly and warmly without pet names: endearments such as 'love' appear at most once per stop and often not at all. She never lectures; she points, remembers, and moves you along. Her knowledge, prices and worries come from the street sellers interviewed in Henry Mayhew's London Labour and the London Poor (1851). She knows nothing after spring 1850 and has never been past Greenwich or Kensington.

style.look: Photographic realism as if a large-format camera had been on the spot in 1850, natural overcast London light, wet cobbles, coal smoke haze, period-correct clothing (women in shawls and bonnets, men in top hats or caps, no bare heads), horse traffic only, gas lamps, painted shop signs. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level from the pavement. Muted colour, not sepia. No text overlays, no watermarks.
style.avoid: no modern vehicles, no electric lights, no railway bridge across Ludgate Hill (built 1865), no Tower Bridge (1894), no modern clothing, no bicycles, no cartoon or painterly styles, no faces of real named historical figures

stops.title: Ludgate Hill
stops.brief: The busiest street in the City, climbing east to St Paul's. Omnibuses, drays, hand-carts, crossing-sweepers, the cathedral dome filling the end of the street. Nell's pitch is on the north pavement near the churchyard railings.

stops.title: St Paul's Churchyard
stops.brief: The steps and the churchyard: booksellers of Paternoster Row behind, the drapers and warehouses, the cathedral itself. Where Nell does her best trade with clerks and visitors. Money, prices, what a day earns.
mustCover: what she pays at Covent Garden and what she sells for
a day's takings in good and bad weather
what a loaf and a pint cost
the clerks and the shopmen

stops.title: Paternoster Row
stops.brief: The narrow street of booksellers and publishers north of the cathedral. Cheap print, penny papers, ballad sheets. Reading and not reading. News of the day: the Exhibition being built, the Queen, the price of bread.
mustCover: the penny press and what people read aloud
news of 1850 as a street seller hears it
the Great Exhibition being built in Hyde Park

stops.title: Fleet Street and the Fleet Ditch
stops.brief: Down the hill: newspaper offices, taverns, Temple Bar ahead. Under the road runs the buried Fleet river, a sewer. Smell, cholera, water. Where the coffee-stalls are.
mustCover: the smell and the buried river
cholera of 1849 and fear of its return
coffee-stall prices and who drinks there
Temple Bar

stops.title: Blackfriars Bridge
stops.brief: South to the river. The old stone Blackfriars Bridge (replaced 1869), the tide, the wherries and steamers, the smell of the Thames, the mudlarks on the foreshore at low water.
mustCover: the river as a road: penny steamers and wherries
mudlarks and what they find
the Thames as the city's drain

stops.title: The foreshore at low tide
stops.brief: Down on the stones at low water below the wharves. Looking back up at the dome above the warehouses. Where Nell says goodbye: what she hopes for Tom and Sal, and what the city will do next.
mustCover: what she hopes for her children
how far she has travelled in her life
